subject.title: fix(cli): block embedded fallback for gateway-accepted agent turns on transport error

question: Should post-acceptance Gateway transport loss permanently return an in-flight result, or should OpenClaw preserve fallback only after a confirmed abort of the accepted run?
rationale: The patch removes an existing fallback outcome to prevent duplicate side effects, but that intentionally changes the CLI timeout contract for established scripts and operators.

options.title: Adopt single-execution semantics
options.body: Land the in-flight-result approach after direct CLI proof, making accepted Gateway runs authoritative and requiring callers to reattach or extend their timeout.

options.title: Require confirmed abort before fallback
options.body: Preserve a fallback response only when the CLI can confirm that the accepted Gateway run was aborted first.

options.title: Keep current behavior temporarily
options.body: Defer the contract change and retain the existing fallback until an owner-approved compatibility plan is available.

recommendation.title: Adopt single-execution semantics
recommendation.body: Land the in-flight-result approach after direct CLI proof, making accepted Gateway runs authoritative and requiring callers to reattach or extend their timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely core CLI decision owner for an intentional compatibility change in the gateway-to-embedded execution boundary.
